claims: C1 user and developer messages are treated interchangeably
C2 when both are present in a conversation, developer messages have greater authority
C3 when user/developer conflicts are not relevant and there is no risk of confusion, the word 'user' is sometimes used as shorthand for 'user or developer'

concepts.name: user_message
concepts.gloss: M is a message supplied by a user of a product made by OpenAI or a third-party application built on the OpenAI API

concepts.name: developer_message
concepts.gloss: M is a message supplied by a developer, a customer of the OpenAI API who may add intelligence to software applications or create natural language interfaces consumed by end users

concepts.name: message_in_conversation
concepts.gloss: message M is present in conversation C
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of messages being present in a conversation, so a relation between a message and a conversation must exist

concepts.name: greater_authority
concepts.gloss: message M has greater authority than message N in the conversation

concepts.name: conversation_with_both
concepts.gloss: a conversation in which at least one user message and at least one developer message are both present
concepts.inference: the clause's exception condition 'when both are present in a conversation' requires a class of conversations containing both kinds of message

concepts.name: no_conflict_no_confusion
concepts.gloss: a context in which user/developer conflicts are not relevant and there is no risk of confusion

concepts.name: user_shorthand
concepts.gloss: a use of the word 'user' in the spec that is shorthand for 'user or developer'

concepts.name: user_definition
concepts.gloss: a user of a product made by OpenAI or a third-party application built on the OpenAI API

concepts.name: developer_definition
concepts.gloss: a customer of the OpenAI API who may add intelligence to software applications or create natural language interfaces consumed by end users

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts

ontology.gloss: C is a conversation containing both a user message and a developer message
ontology.body: message_in_conversation(M1, C), user_message(M1), message_in_conversation(M2, C), developer_message(M2)

ontology.gloss: U is a use of the word 'user' that is shorthand for 'user or developer' because user/developer conflicts are not relevant and there is no risk of confusion
